subtopic: Conditional Probability and the Multiplication Theorem
stem: A bag contains 3 red marbles and 4 blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random without replacement. If the first marble drawn is red, what is the probability the second marble is blue?
solution: [Textbook answer-key error: the printed key gives \(\dfrac{2}{7}\), which is the JOINT probability \(P(R_1 \cap B_2) = \dfrac{3}{7} \times \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{7}\) — the chance that the first marble is red AND the second is blue. The question as printed states that the first marble drawn IS red, so it asks for the conditional probability, and with 2 red and 4 blue left in the bag that is \(\dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\). The stem was checked word for word against the printed page; the key answers a question the stem does not ask.]

subtopic: Conditional Probability and the Multiplication Theorem
stem: A bag contains 6 red, 5 blue balls and another bag contains 5 red and 8 blue balls. A ball is drawn from first bag and without noticing colour is put in the second bag. A ball is drawn from the second bag. Find the probability that ball drawn is blue in colour.
solution:
[Textbook misprint: the last line of the printed solution reads \(\left(\dfrac{48}{154}\right)\left(\dfrac{45}{154}\right) = \dfrac{93}{154}\) — the \(+\) between the two fractions is missing, so as printed it reads as a product. The stated answer \(\dfrac{93}{154}\) is correct and is their SUM.]

Let event \(E_1\): Red ball is drawn from the first bag and event \(E_2\): Blue ball is drawn from the first bag.

\(\therefore P(E_1) = \frac{6}{11}\) and \(P(E_2) = \frac{5}{11}\) (Note that \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) are mutually exclusive and exhaustive events)

Let event A: Blue ball is drawn from the second bag

\(\therefore P(A/E_1) = P\)(Blue ball is drawn from the second under the condition that red ball is transferred from first bag to second bag) \(= \frac{8}{14}\)

Similarly, \(P(A/E_2) = P\)(Blue ball is drawn from the second under the condition that blue ball is transferred from first bag to second bag) \(= \frac{9}{14}\)

\(\therefore\) required probability \(= P\)(Blue ball is drawn from the second bag)

\(\therefore P(A) = P(A \cap E_1) + P(A \cap E_2)\)

\(= P(E_1)P(A/E_1) + P(E_2)P(A/E_2)\)

\(= \left(\frac{6}{11}\right)\left(\frac{8}{14}\right) + \left(\frac{5}{11}\right)\left(\frac{9}{14}\right)\)

\(= \left(\frac{48}{154}\right)\left(\frac{45}{154}\right) = \frac{93}{154}\)
_note: TWO printed defects on p-15 (printed p.208). (1) The stem prints "6 red, 5blue balls" with no space; transcribed as "5 blue". (2) BOOK MISPRINT in the last line of the printed solution: it reads \(= \left(\frac{48}{154}\right)\left(\frac{45}{154}\right) = \frac{93}{154}\) — the PLUS sign between the two fractions is missing, so as printed it reads as a product. Verified at 3x zoom: the "+" is clearly present on the line above (\(\left(\frac{6}{11}\right)\left(\frac{8}{14}\right) + \left(\frac{5}{11}\right)\left(\frac{9}{14}\right)\)) and clearly ABSENT on this one. The final answer \(\frac{93}{154}\) is correct and follows from \(\frac{48}{154} + \frac{45}{154}\). Transcribed exactly as printed; NOT silently repaired.

subtopic: Bayes' Theorem
stem: The chances of X, Y, Z becoming managers of a certain company are 4:2:3. The probabilities that the bonus scheme will be introduced if X, Y, Z become managers are 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8 respectively. If the bonus scheme has been introduced, what is the probability that X is appointed as the manager?
solution:
Let \(E_1\): Person X becomes manager

\(E_2\): Person Y becomes manager

Let \(E_3\): Person Z becomes manager

\(\therefore P(E_1) = \frac{4}{9}\); \(P(E_2) = \frac{2}{9}\); \(P(E_3) = \frac{3}{9}\)

(Note that \(E_1\), \(E_2\) and \(E_3\) are mutually exclusive and exhaustive events)

Let event A: Bonus is introduced.

\(\therefore P(A/E_1) = P\)(Bonus is introduced under the condition that person X becomes manager) \(= 0.3\)

\(P(A/E_2) = P\)(Bonus is introduced under the condition that person Y becomes manager) \(= 0.5\)

and \(P(A/E_3) = P\)(Bonus is introduced under the condition that person Z becomes manager) \(= 0.8\)

\(\therefore P(A) = P(A \cap E_1) + P(A \cap E_2) + P(A \cap E_3)\)

\(= P(E_1)P(A/E_1) + P(E_2)P(A/E_2) + P(E_3)P(A/E_3)\)

\(= \left(\frac{4}{9}\right)(0.3) + \left(\frac{2}{9}\right)(0.5) + \left(\frac{3}{9}\right)(0.8)\)

\(= \frac{23}{45}\)

\(\therefore\) required probability \(= P\)(Person X becomes manager under the condition that bonus scheme is introduced)

\(= P(E_1/A) = P(A \cap E_1) / P(A)\)

\(= \frac{(2/15)}{(23/45)}\)

\(= \frac{6}{23}\)
_note: The book prints "what is the probability that X is appointed as the manger?" — misspelling of "manager"; transcribed with the spelling corrected. The printed solution jumps from \(P(A) = \frac{23}{45}\) straight to \(\frac{(2/15)}{(23/45)}\) without showing that \(P(A \cap E_1) = \left(\frac{4}{9}\right)(0.3) = \frac{2}{15}\); the value is correct.

subtopic: Bayes' Theorem
stem: The members of the consulting firm hire cars from three rental agencies, 60% from agency X, 30% from agency Y and 10% from agency Z. 9% of the cars from agency X need repairs, 20% of the cars from agency Y need repairs and 6% of the cars from agency Z need repairs. If a rental car delivered to the consulting firms needs repairs, what is the probability that it came from rental agency Y?
solution:
If A is the event that the car needs repairs and B, C, D are the events that the car comes from rental agencies X, Y or Z. We have \(P(B) = 0.6\), \(P(C) = 0.3\), \(P(D) = 0.1\), \(P(A/B) = 0.09\), \(P(A/C) = 0.2\) and \(P(A/D) = 0.06\)

\(P(A) = P(A \cap B) + P(A \cap C) + P(A \cap D)\)

\(= P(B).P(A/B) + P(C).P(A/C) + P(D).P(A/D)\)

\(= 0.6 \times 0.09 + 0.3 \times 0.2 + 0.1 \times 0.06\)

\(= 0.054 + 0.06 + 0.006\)

\(\therefore P(A) = 0.12\)

\(P(C/A) = \frac{P(A \cap C)}{P(A)} = \frac{P(C).P(A/C)}{P(A)}\)

\(= \frac{0.3 \times 0.2}{0.12} = \frac{0.06}{0.12}\)

\(= 0.5\)
_note: The stem begins on p-15 (printed p.208, bottom of right column) and continues onto p-16 (printed p.209, top of left column); the whole printed solution is on p-16, ending at \(= 0.5\) immediately before the EXERCISE 9.4 banner. Re-derived and correct as printed.
